scope: Six current no-road environment concept boards only; historical 01–04, human/building art, all Blender files, Unity and gameplay unchanged.
prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather
Asset type: edited medieval-apocalypse RTS wilderness concept sheet, NOT a Unity screenshot or PBR texture.
Input image: edit target, existing road-free environment board.
Primary request: Make this EXACT scene moderately cooler, darker, more somber and ominous: an abandoned wilderness suitable for zombie-survival RTS, informed by the oppressive readable terrain mood of They Are Billions, without copying its assets. Replace cheerful golden daytime illumination with dim diffuse overcast daylight, subtle cool slate-grey atmospheric distance and deeper contact shadows. Remove luminous sunny yellow/lime foliage; use muted olive-grey and grey-green vegetation with dark wooded interiors. Stone reads cool neutral grey; water darker desaturated blue-green, NOT holiday turquoise. Maintain detailed textured midtones and clear land-water-cliff boundaries for RTS gameplay; exposure only moderately lower, blacks must retain detail, no dark vignette, no blanket blue filter, no pure-white wash. Retain restrained natural earth-brown warmth, dry grass straw-brown and desert sand beige/grey ochre where appropriate: deserts must remain geographically distinct, not turn into blue tundra. No glowing effects or invented darkness props.
Invariants: Preserve exact camera, perspective, terrain forms and elevations, tree/plant species, water bodies, coastline, asset silhouettes, sheet composition, isolated bottom studies and swatch layout. Apply same coherent cooler material/light treatment to inset studies. ONLY revise light/mood/material color balance, no new objects. Preserve NO human tracks/roads/wheel ruts/paving, NO rivers, NO buildings/units/bones/ruins/gravestones or extra props. Do not add new water. No labels, text, watermark or UI. Crisp rich 3D-like detail, natural readable shadow transitions, not a blurry or monochrome scene.
For the North African/desert boards specifically, preserve weathered sandstone as grey-beige/soft muted ochre (not blue slate); keep sand natural grey-beige. For temperate/alpine boards, neutral grey rock may have cool slate shadows.

research.evidence: Actual official trailer and screenshot viewed in browser: muted olive/brown ground, cold snow/blue notes, warm window lights, bright yellow-beige desert and orange fire. Visual inference, not measured grading values or a claim that all maps are uniformly cold.
Developer describes detailed art with a hand-drawn touch and an oppressive surrounding-infected atmosphere.

palette_decision: Reduce sunny gold/lime; diffuse overcast, olive/grey-green plants, deeper legible shadows, grey rock, darker blue-green water. Preserve soil/straw/desert beige/ochre. No global monochrome-blue/night blackout.
visual_review: Root and independent art specialist inspected all six: moderate colder/darker treatment, no major composition deformation, no added roads/rivers, plant/rock/water boundaries and lower studies remain readable. Pond09 is darkest: do not reduce exposure further without user preference.
preservation: Brighter v2 and original files preserved; human/building warmth is unchanged.
